Chapter 8: Building Confidence Through Action—Trusting Yourself to Decide
You know, one of the biggest reasons we get stuck in overthinking is because we just don’t trust our own judgment enough. Our minds start hesitating, searching for more info, wanting reassurance... and then, before we know it, we’re putting off decisions or avoiding them altogether.
But here’s the thing—there’s a way out. And it’s all about building confidence through action. That means making choices, learning from what happens, and slowly but surely, teaching yourself to trust your own instincts.
Now, confidence doesn’t mean you’re never going to feel doubt. Instead, it’s about being willing to take action, even when you’re not totally sure how things will turn out.
Every time you make a decision and follow through, you’re showing your mind that you can handle whatever comes next. Even if things don’t go perfectly, you learn something. That feedback is so valuable—and it makes you more resilient the next time around.
So how can you start building that decision-making confidence in everyday life?
Here are some simple ideas you can try:
First, start small. Practice making quick decisions about things that aren’t a big deal. Like, what are you going to eat for lunch? Which book will you read next? Or even, which route will you take home today? When you pay attention, you’ll notice that most choices are totally reversible—and they rarely have long-lasting consequences.
Next, try setting time limits for yourself. Give yourself, say, five minutes to decide. This keeps you from getting stuck in endless back-and-forth, and helps you build the habit of taking action.
Another helpful trick? Reflect on your past successes. Think back to times you made good decisions—even if you were uncertain back then. Remind yourself: you’ve done it before, and you can do it again.
Let’s imagine someone who always agonizes over social invitations. They’re afraid of making the “wrong” choice, so they go back and forth, feeling anxious. But what if they set a deadline—“I’ll decide by 6 p.m.”—and remembered all the fun times they had when they trusted themselves? With that small shift, they could choose with a lot less stress and a lot more confidence.
Building confidence is a process—you take it one step at a time. Every small act of deciding, paired with a little self-compassion, makes your belief in yourself stronger. Over time, that self-trust becomes a powerful shield against overthinking.
So, next time you catch yourself hesitating, remember: action is the antidote. Trust yourself to decide, and watch your confidence grow.
